questions.questionText: If the speed of swimmer is 9 km/hr in still water and the speed of stream is 5 km/hr then find the speed of swimmer against the stream and along the stream.
questions.solution: Speed against stream (upstream) $= u - v = 9 - 5 = 4\text{ km/hr}$.\nSpeed along stream (downstream) $= u + v = 9 + 5 = 14\text{ km/hr}$.

questions.questionText: If the speed of a boat in still water is 3 km/h and if its upstream speed is 1 km/h, find the speed of the stream.
questions.solution: Upstream speed $= u - v = 1\text{ km/h}$.\nGiven $u = 3\text{ km/h} \implies 3 - v = 1 \implies v = 2\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A boatman rows 2 km in 10 min., along the stream and 12 km in 2 hrs against the stream. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.solution: Downstream speed $D = \frac{2}{10/60} = 12\text{ km/h}$.\nUpstream speed $U = \frac{12}{2} = 6\text{ km/h}$.\nSpeed of stream $v = \frac{D - U}{2} = \frac{12 - 6}{2} = 3\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A boat covers a distance of 55 km downstream in 5 hours while it takes 11 hours to cover the same distance upstream. What is the speed of the boat?
questions.solution: Downstream speed $D = \frac{55}{5} = 11\text{ km/h}$.\nUpstream speed $U = \frac{55}{11} = 5\text{ km/h}$.\nSpeed of boat in still water $u = \frac{D + U}{2} = \frac{11 + 5}{2} = 8\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: The speed of a boat when travelling downstream is 33 km/h, whereas when travelling upstream it is 27 km/h. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution: Speed of boat in still water $= \frac{D + U}{2} = \frac{33 + 27}{2} = 30\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: The speed of a boat when travelling downstream is 48 km/h, whereas when travelling upstream it is 32 km/h. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution: Speed of boat in still water $= \frac{D + U}{2} = \frac{48 + 32}{2} = 40\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: Two boats move downstream in a river at the speed of 35 km/hr and 25 km/hr. The speed of the stream is 4 km/hr. Initially the distance between the two boats is 60 km. If both the boats are moving downstream, in what time will they meet each other?
questions.solution: Relative speed between the two boats $= 35 - 25 = 10\text{ km/hr}$.\nTime to meet $= \frac{60}{10} = 6\text{ hours}$.

questions.questionText: The ratio of the speeds of a boat while going upstream and going downstream is 2 : 3 and the sum of these two speeds is 15 km/h. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.solution: Let $U = 2x, D = 3x$. Sum $= 2x + 3x = 5x = 15 \implies x = 3$.\n$U = 6\text{ km/h}, D = 9\text{ km/h}$.\nSpeed of stream $v = \frac{9 - 6}{2} = 1.5\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A boat running upstream takes 10 hours to cover a certain distance, while it takes 7 hours to cover the same distance running downstream. What is the ratio between the speed of the boat and that of the water current respectively?
questions.solution: Distance $d = (u - v) \times 10 = (u + v) \times 7 \implies 10u - 10v = 7u + 7v \implies 3u = 17v \implies \frac{u}{v} = \frac{17}{3}$.

questions.questionText: The speed of a boat in still water is $5\frac{1}{3}\text{ km/h}$. It is found that the boat takes thrice as much time to row up than it does to row down the same distance in the river stream. Find the speed of the river stream.
questions.solution: Given $u = \frac{16}{3}\text{ km/h}$. Since $t_{up} = 3 t_{down} \implies u + v = 3(u - v) \implies 2u = 4v \implies v = \frac{u}{2} = \frac{16}{6} = \frac{8}{3}\text{ km/h}$.\nIn m/sec: $\frac{8}{3} \times \frac{5}{18} = \frac{20}{27}\text{ m/sec}$.

questions.questionText: A man can row 18 km/h in still water. It takes him two times as long to row up as to row down the river. Find the rate of the stream.
questions.solution: $u + v = 2(u - v) \implies u = 3v \implies v = \frac{18}{3} = 6\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A man can row a boat at speed of 8 km/h in still water. It takes thrice as long to row upstream as it does to row downstream. Find the speed of the stream (in km/h).
questions.solution: $u + v = 3(u - v) \implies 2u = 4v \implies v = \frac{u}{2} = \frac{8}{2} = 4\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: The time taken by a boat to cover a distance of x km upstream is double the time taken by the boat to cover the same distance downstream. The sum of the speeds of the boat and the stream is 90 km/h. The speed of the stream is ___ km/h.
questions.solution: Downstream speed $D = u + v = 90\text{ km/h}$.\nSince $U = \frac{D}{2} = 45\text{ km/h} \implies u - v = 45$.\nSpeed of stream $v = \frac{90 - 45}{2} = 22.5\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A man rows to a place 48 km distant and comes back in 14 hours. He finds that he can row 4 km with the stream in the same time as 3 km against the stream. The speed of the stream is:
questions.solution: $\frac{D}{U} = \frac{4}{3} \implies D = 4k, U = 3k$. $u = 3.5k, v = 0.5k$.\nTotal time $= \frac{48}{4k} + \frac{48}{3k} = \frac{12}{k} + \frac{16}{k} = \frac{28}{k} = 14 \implies k = 2$.\n$D = 8\text{ km/h}, U = 6\text{ km/h} \implies v = \frac{8 - 6}{2} = 1\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: The speed of a boat downstream is 2.5 times the speed of the boat upstream. If the time taken by the boat for going 30 km downstream and the same distance upstream is 7 hours, then what is the speed (in km/h) of the boat downstream?
questions.solution: Let $U = y, D = 2.5y$.\n$\frac{30}{2.5y} + \frac{30}{y} = \frac{12}{y} + \frac{30}{y} = \frac{42}{y} = 7 \implies y = 6\text{ km/h}$.\nDownstream speed $= 2.5 \times 6 = 15\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: The speed of a boat downstream is 150% more than its speed upstream. If the time taken by the boat for going 80km downstream and 50km upstream is 8.2 hours, then what is the speed (in km/h) of the boat downstream?
questions.solution: $D = U + 1.5U = 2.5U \implies \frac{D}{U} = \frac{5}{2}$. Let $D = 5x, U = 2x$.\n$\frac{80}{5x} + \frac{50}{2x} = \frac{16}{x} + \frac{25}{x} = \frac{41}{x} = 8.2 \implies x = 5$.\nDownstream speed $= 5 \times 5 = 25\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: The speed of the boat in downstream is 125% of the speed of the boat in still water. If the boat takes 30 minutes to cover a distance of 20 km in still water, then how much time (in hours) will it take to cover a distance of 15 km upstream?
questions.solution:
Speed in still water $u =  rac{20}{30/60} = 40	ext{ km/h}$.
$D = 1.25 	imes 40 = 50	ext{ km/h} \implies v = 10	ext{ km/h}$.
$U = 40 - 10 = 30	ext{ km/h}$.
Time for 15 km upstream $=  rac{15}{30} =  rac{1}{2}	ext{ hours}$.

questions.questionText: The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream is 8 : 3 and the boat can travel 22 km downstream in 24 minutes. Then, how much time will the boat take to cover 50 km upstream?
questions.solution:
$u : v = 8 : 3 \implies D = 11x, U = 5x$.
$D =  rac{22}{24/60} = 55	ext{ km/h} \implies 11x = 55 \implies x = 5$.
$U = 5 	imes 5 = 25	ext{ km/h}$.
Time to cover 50 km upstream $=  rac{50}{25} = 2	ext{ hours}$.

questions.questionText: A boat travels 5 km upstream in 15 minutes. If the ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream is 6 : 1, then how much time will the boat take to cover a distance of 19.6 km in down stream? (in minutes)
questions.solution:
$U =  rac{5}{15/60} = 20	ext{ km/h}$.
$u : v = 6 : 1 \implies U = 5x = 20 \implies x = 4$.
$D = 6x + 1x = 7x = 28	ext{ km/h}$.
Time for 19.6 km downstream $=  rac{19.6}{28} 	imes 60 = 42	ext{ minutes}$.

questions.questionText: The speed of a boat in still water is 25 km/h. It takes $33\frac{1}{3}\%$ more time to cover a certain distance in still water than to cover the same distance downstream. How much time in hours will boat take to go 75 km downstream?
questions.solution: $33\frac{1}{3}\% = \frac{1}{3} \implies \frac{t_{still}}{t_{down}} = \frac{4}{3} \implies \frac{D}{u} = \frac{4}{3} \implies D = \frac{4}{3} \times 25 = \frac{100}{3}\text{ km/h}$.\nTime to go 75 km downstream $= \frac{75}{100/3} = 2.25\text{ hours}$.

questions.questionText: A boatman rows to a place 30 km distance and back in 14 hours. He finds that he can row 10 km with the stream at the same time as 4 km against the stream. Find the speed (in km/h) of the stream.
questions.solution: $\frac{D}{U} = \frac{10}{4} = \frac{5}{2} \implies D = 5k, U = 2k$.\n$\frac{30}{5k} + \frac{30}{2k} = 14 \implies \frac{6}{k} + \frac{15}{k} = 14 \implies \frac{21}{k} = 14 \implies k = \frac{3}{2}$.\nSpeed of stream $v = \frac{D - U}{2} = \frac{3k}{2} = \frac{3 \times 1.5}{2} = \frac{9}{4}\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A man rows 48 km and back in 48 hrs. He can row 4 km with the stream in the same time as 3 km against the stream. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is:
questions.solution: $\frac{D}{U} = \frac{4}{3} \implies D = 4k, U = 3k$.\n$\frac{48}{4k} + \frac{48}{3k} = 48 \implies \frac{12}{k} + \frac{16}{k} = 48 \implies \frac{28}{k} = 48 \implies k = \frac{7}{12}$.\nSpeed of stream $v = \frac{4k - 3k}{2} = \frac{k}{2} = \frac{7}{24}\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: Ashu can row 7.5 km an hour in still water. He finds that it takes four times as much time to row upstream, as it takes to row downstream. The speed of the stream is:
questions.solution: $u + v = 4(u - v) \implies 3u = 5v \implies v = \frac{3 \times 7.5}{5} = 4.5\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A man wishes to cover 1 km distance in river water. In still water he takes 12 minutes to cover it, but in the flowing river he takes 13 minutes. The speed of the flowing water of the river is:
questions.solution: $u = \frac{1}{12/60} = 5\text{ km/h}$. Against stream $U = \frac{1}{13/60} = \frac{60}{13}\text{ km/h}$.\n$v = u - U = 5 - \frac{60}{13} = \frac{5}{13}\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A boat can travel 60km downstream in 4 hours. If the speed of the boat in still water is 13 km/h, then in what time will it cover 30 km upstream?
questions.solution: $D = 60/4 = 15\text{ km/h} \implies v = 15 - 13 = 2\text{ km/h}$.\n$U = 13 - 2 = 11\text{ km/h}$. Time for 30 km $= \frac{30}{11} = 2\frac{8}{11}\text{ hours}$.

questions.questionText: A boat can travel with a speed of 19 km/h in still water. If the speed of the stream is 3 km/h, then what will be the total time (in hours) taken by the boat to go 88 km downstream and 24 km upstream?
A person can row 5m/sec in still water. The speed of the stream is 6 km/h. The time (in hours) taken by him to row a distance of 76.8 km downstream is:
questions.solution: $u = 5 \times \frac{18}{5} = 18\text{ km/h}$. $D = 18 + 6 = 24\text{ km/h}$.\nTime $= \frac{76.8}{24} = 3.2\text{ hours}$.

questions.questionText: Sunil can row a boat 20 km upstream in 1 hour 15 minutes. If the speed of the current of the river is 2 km/h, then how much time will he take to row the boat 30 km downstream?
questions.solution: $U = \frac{20}{5/4} = 16\text{ km/h} \implies u = 16 + 2 = 18\text{ km/h}$.\n$D = 18 + 2 = 20\text{ km/h}$. Time $= \frac{30}{20} = 1.5\text{ hr} = 1\text{ hr } 30\text{ min}$.

questions.questionText: A boat can go 54 km upstream in 6 hours. If the speed of the stream is 4.8 km/h, then how much time (in hours) will the boat take to cover a distance of 279 km downstream?
A boat can travel 16.9 km downstream in 52 min. If the speed of the current is 3 km/h, then how much time (in hours) will the boat take to travel 84 km upstream?
questions.solution: $D = \frac{16.9}{52/60} = 19.5\text{ km/h} \implies u = 16.5\text{ km/h}$.\n$U = 16.5 - 3 = 13.5\text{ km/h}$. Time $= \frac{84}{13.5} \approx 6.22\text{ hours}$.

questions.questionText: A boatman goes 2 km against the current of the stream in 1 hour and goes 1 km along with the current in 10 minutes. How long will it take to go 6 km in still water?
questions.solution: $U = 2\text{ km/h}, D = \frac{1}{1/6} = 6\text{ km/h} \implies u = \frac{6 + 2}{2} = 4\text{ km/h}$.\nTime for 6 km $= \frac{6}{4} = 1.5\text{ hr} = 1\text{ hr } 30\text{ min}$.

questions.questionText: Time taken by a boat to go a certain distance upstream is twice the time taken by it to go the same distance downstream. If the speed of the stream is 3 km/h, then how much time in hours will the boat take to go 52 km upstream?
questions.solution: $u + v = 2(u - v) \implies u = 3v = 9\text{ km/h}$.\n$U = 9 - 3 = 6\text{ km/h}$. Time $= \frac{52}{6} = 8\frac{2}{3}\text{ hours}$.

questions.questionText: A man can row a distance of 6 km in 1 hour in still water. He can row the same distance in 45 minutes with the current. Find the total time taken by him to row a distance of 16 km with the current and to return to the starting point.
questions.solution: $u = 6, D = \frac{6}{3/4} = 8\text{ km/h} \implies v = 2\text{ km/h}, U = 4\text{ km/h}$.\nTotal time $= \frac{16}{8} + \frac{16}{4} = 2 + 4 = 6\text{ hours}$.

questions.questionText: A man takes 15 minutes to row 16 km downstream, which is 25% less than the time he takes to row the same distance upstream. How many kilometers can the man row in an hour in still water? (Rounded off to nearest whole number)
questions.solution: $t_{down} = 15\text{ min} = 0.75 t_{up} \implies t_{up} = 20\text{ min}$.\n$D = \frac{16}{15/60} = 64\text{ km/h}, U = \frac{16}{20/60} = 48\text{ km/h}$.\n$u = \frac{64 + 48}{2} = 56\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: Time taken by boat to cover a distance of x km in upstream is 3 hrs more than the time taken by the boat to cover the same distance in downstream. Speed of the boat in upstream is 8 km/hr. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?\nI. If the value of x is 48 km, then speed of boat in downstream is 16 km/hr.\nII. If the speed of boat in downstream is 12 km/hr, then the value of x is 48 km.
questions.solution: If $x = 48$, $t_{up} = 48/8 = 6$ hrs $\implies t_{down} = 3$ hrs $\implies D = 48/3 = 16\text{ km/hr}$ (Statement I is correct).\nIf $D = 12$, $\frac{x}{8} - \frac{x}{12} = 3 \implies x = 72\text{ km}$ (Statement II is incorrect). Hence, Only I.

questions.questionText: A boat covers a certain distance downstream in 2 hours, while it comes back in $2\frac{1}{2}$ hours. If the speed of the stream is 3 km/h, then what is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution: $\frac{u}{v} = \frac{2.5 + 2}{2.5 - 2} = \frac{4.5}{0.5} = 9 \implies u = 9 \times 3 = 27\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A motorboat takes 18 hours to go downstream, and it takes 36 hours to return the same distance. Find the ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream.

A boat takes 11 hours to travel a distance upstream and takes 5 hours to travel the same distance downstream. if the speed of the boat in still water is $2\frac{2}{9}\text{ m/sec}$, then the speed of the stream (in km/h)is:
questions.solution: $u = \frac{20}{9} \times \frac{18}{5} = 8\text{ km/h}$. $\frac{u}{v} = \frac{11 + 5}{11 - 5} = \frac{16}{6} = \frac{8}{3} \implies v = 3\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: The ratio of the speed of a boat to that of the current water is 35 : 8. The boat goes along with the current in 5 hours 10 minutes. What will be the time taken by the boat to come back?
questions.solution: $D = 35 + 8 = 43, U = 35 - 8 = 27$.\n$t_{up} = \frac{43}{27} \times 310\text{ min} = 493.7\text{ min} = 8\text{ hr } 13\text{ min } 48\text{ sec}$.

questions.questionText: The ratio of the speed of a motorboat to that of the current of water is 31:6. The motorboat starts from a point and covers a certain distance along the current in 4 h 10 min. Find the time taken by the motorboat to come back to its initial point.
questions.solution: $D = 31 + 6 = 37, U = 31 - 6 = 25$.\n$t_{up} = \frac{37}{25} \times 250\text{ min} = 370\text{ min} = 6\text{ h } 10\text{ min}$.

questions.questionText: The speed of a boat in still water is thrice the speed of the stream. If the boat takes 15.5 sec to go to a certain place downstream, then find the additional time required to cover the same distance travelling upstream.
questions.solution: $u = 3v \implies D = 4v, U = 2v \implies t_{up} = 2 \times t_{down} = 31\text{ sec}$.\nAdditional time $= 31 - 15.5 = 15.5\text{ sec}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: BASED ON: T = (2 * D * x) / (x^2 - y^2)
questions.questionText: A motorboat, whose speed in 15 km/h in still water goes 50 km downstream and comes back in a total of 7 hours 30 minutes. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is?
questions.solution: $\frac{50}{15+v} + \frac{50}{15-v} = 7.5 \implies \frac{50 \times 30}{225 - v^2} = \frac{15}{2} \implies \frac{100}{225 - v^2} = \frac{1}{2} \implies 225 - v^2 = 200 \implies v^2 = 25 \implies v = 5\text{ km/h}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: BASED ON: T = (2 * D * x) / (x^2 - y^2)
questions.questionText: A motorboat, whose speed is 20 km/h in still water goes 75 km downstream and comes back in a total of 8 hours. The speed of the stream is:
questions.solution: $\frac{75}{20+v} + \frac{75}{20-v} = 8$. Testing $v = 5$: $\frac{75}{25} + \frac{75}{15} = 3 + 5 = 8\text{ hours}$. Hence $v = 5\text{ km/h}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: BASED ON: T = (2 * D * x) / (x^2 - y^2)
questions.questionText: The speed of boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the current is 6 km/h. In how much time (in hours) will the boat travel a distance of 90 km upstream and the same distance downstream?

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: BASED ON: T = (2 * D * x) / (x^2 - y^2)
questions.questionText: A man can row 5 km/h in still water. If the speed of the current is 2.5 km/h, it takes 4 hours more in upstream than in the downstream for the same distance. The distance is:
questions.solution: $D_{down} = 5 + 2.5 = 7.5\text{ km/h}, U_{up} = 5 - 2.5 = 2.5\text{ km/h}$.\n$\frac{d}{2.5} - \frac{d}{7.5} = 4 \implies \frac{2d}{7.5} = 4 \implies d = 15\text{ km}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: BASED ON: D = T * (B^2 - S^2) / (2B)
questions.questionText: A motorboat, whose speed is 15 km/h in still water goes 20 km downstream and comes back in a total of 4 hours. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is:
questions.solution: $\frac{20}{15+v} + \frac{20}{15-v} = 4 \implies \frac{20 \times 30}{225 - v^2} = 4 \implies 225 - v^2 = 150 \implies v^2 = 75 \implies v = 5\sqrt{3}\text{ km/h}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: BASED ON: D = T * (B^2 - S^2) / (2B)
questions.questionText: In a stream running at 3 km/h, a motorboat goes 12 km upstream and back to the starting point in 60 min. Find the speed of the motorboat in still water, (in km/h)

questions.questionText: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. How much time (in hours) will it take to cover a distance of 105 km in downstream and in coming back?

questions.questionText: The speed of a boat in still water is 12 km/h, and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. A man goes to a place by boat, 45 km and comes back to the starting point. Find the total time taken by him.

questions.questionText: The speed of a boat in a still river is 15 km/h and the speed of the current is 5 km/h. In what time (in hours) will the boat cover a distance of 60 kilometers downstream and the same distance upstream?

questions.questionText: The speed of a boat in standing water is 6 km/h and the speed of the stream is 2.5 km/h. A man rows to a place at a distance of 59.5 km and comes back to the starting point. The total time taken by him is:

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: BASED ON: D = T * (B^2 - S^2) / (2B)
questions.questionText: A boat racer can row $21\frac{3}{2}\text{ km/h}$ in still water. If the speed of river is 12.5 km/h, it takes him 40 minutes to row to a place and back, how far off is the place (consider up to two decimals)?
questions.solution: Speed in still water $u = 21 + 1.5 = 22.5\text{ km/h}, v = 12.5\text{ km/h}$.\n$D = 22.5 + 12.5 = 35\text{ km/h}, U = 22.5 - 12.5 = 10\text{ km/h}$.\n$\frac{d}{35} + \frac{d}{10} = \frac{40}{60} = \frac{2}{3} \implies \frac{2d + 7d}{70} = \frac{2}{3} \implies \frac{9d}{70} = \frac{2}{3} \implies d = \frac{140}{27} = 5\frac{5}{27}\text{ km}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: BASED ON: D = T * (B^2 - S^2) / (2B)
questions.questionText: The speed of a boat in still water is 20 km/h, while the river is flowing at a speed of 8 km/h and the time taken to cover a certain distance upstream is 6 h more than the time taken to cover the same distance downstream. Find the distance.
questions.solution: $D = 20 + 8 = 28\text{ km/h}, U = 20 - 8 = 12\text{ km/h}$.\n$\frac{d}{12} - \frac{d}{28} = 6 \implies d\left(\frac{7-3}{84}\right) = 6 \implies \frac{4d}{84} = 6 \implies \frac{d}{21} = 6 \implies d = 126\text{ km}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: BASED ON: D = T * (B^2 - S^2) / (2B)
questions.questionText: A motorboat whose speed is 20 km/h in still water takes 30 minutes more to go 24 km upstream than to cover the same distance downstream. If the speed of the boat in still water is increased by 2 km/h, then how much time will it take to go 39 km downstream and 30 km upstream?
questions.solution:
$ rac{24}{20-v} -  rac{24}{20+v} = 0.5 \implies  rac{48v}{400-v^2} =  rac{1}{2} \implies 96v = 400 - v^2 \implies v^2 + 96v - 400 = 0 \implies (v+100)(v-4) = 0 \implies v = 4	ext{ km/h}$.
New still water speed $= 20 + 2 = 22	ext{ km/h}$.
$D_{new} = 22 + 4 = 26	ext{ km/h}, U_{new} = 22 - 4 = 18	ext{ km/h}$.
Time $=  rac{39}{26} +  rac{30}{18} = 1.5 +  rac{5}{3} =  rac{9+10}{6} =  rac{19}{6}	ext{ hours} = 3	ext{ h } 10	ext{ min}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IV: BASED ON: D = T * (B^2 - S^2) / (2B)
questions.questionText: A boat sails downstream from a point P to point Q, Which is 24 km away from P, and then returns to P. If the actual speed of the boat (in still water) is 6 km/h. The entire trip from P to Q taken 3 hours less than what from Q to P. What should be the actual speed (in km/h) of the boat to sail from P to Q in 2 hours?
questions.solution: $\frac{24}{6-v} - \frac{24}{6+v} = 3 \implies \frac{48v}{36-v^2} = 3 \implies 16v = 36-v^2 \implies v^2+16v-36=0 \implies (v+18)(v-2)=0 \implies v = 2\text{ km/h}$.\nTo go 24 km downstream in 2 hours: $D' = \frac{24}{2} = 12\text{ km/h}$.\nSpeed in still water $u' = D' - v = 12 - 2 = 10\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A boat can go 40 km downstream and 25 km upstream in 7 hours 30 minutes. It can go 48 km downstream and 36 km upstream in 10 hours. What is the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
Let downstream speed be $D$ and upstream be $U$.
$40/D + 25/U = 7.5$ and $48/D + 36/U = 10$.
Testing common factors: $D = 16, U = 5$: $40/16 + 25/5 = 2.5 + 5 = 7.5$; $48/16 + 36/5 = 3 + 7.2 = 10.2 
eq 10$.
Testing $D = 12, U = 6$: $48/12 + 36/6 = 4 + 6 = 10$; $40/12 + 25/6 =  rac{105}{12} = 8.75 
eq 7.5$.
Solving system: multiply eq 1 by 6, eq 2 by 5: $240/D + 150/U = 45$ and $240/D + 180/U = 50 \implies 30/U = 5 \implies U = 6	ext{ km/h}$.
Then $40/D + 25/6 = 7.5 \implies 40/D = 7.5 - 4.167 = 3.333 = 10/3 \implies D = 12	ext{ km/h}$.
Speed of boat in still water $u =  rac{D + U}{2} =  rac{12 + 6}{2} = 9	ext{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A motorboat travelling at a certain speed can cover a distance of 24 km upstream and 40 km downstream in 17 hours. At the same speed it can travel 32 km downstream and 12 km upstream in 10 hours. What is the speed of the current?
questions.solution:
$40/D + 24/U = 17$ and $32/D + 12/U = 10$.
Multiply second by 2: $64/D + 24/U = 20$.
Subtract first from this: $24/D = 3 \implies D = 8	ext{ km/h}$.
Then $40/8 + 24/U = 17 \implies 5 + 24/U = 17 \implies 24/U = 12 \implies U = 2	ext{ km/h}$.
Speed of current $v =  rac{D - U}{2} =  rac{8 - 2}{2} = 3	ext{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A boat covers 24 km upstream and 36 km downstream in 10 hours, and 36 km upstream and 24 km down-stream in 12 hours. The speed of the current is:
questions.solution:
$36/D + 24/U = 10$ and $24/D + 36/U = 12$.
Adding: $60(1/D + 1/U) = 22 \implies 1/D + 1/U = 11/30$.
Subtracting: $-12(1/D) + 12(1/U) = 2 \implies 1/U - 1/D = 1/6 = 5/30$.
Adding the two: $2/U = 16/30 \implies 1/U = 4/15 \implies U = 15/4	ext{ km/h}$.
$1/D = 11/30 - 8/30 = 3/30 = 1/10 \implies D = 10	ext{ km/h}$.
Speed of current $v =  rac{D - U}{2} =  rac{10 - 3.75}{2} =  rac{6.25}{2} =  rac{25}{8}	ext{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A boat can go 60 km downstream and 40 km upstream in 12 hours 30 minutes. It can go 84 km downstream and 63 km upstream in 18 hours 54 minutes. What is the speed (in km/h, to the nearest integer) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
$60/D + 40/U = 12.5$ and $84/D + 63/U = 18.9$.
Multiplying first by 7, second by 5: $420/D + 280/U = 87.5$, $420/D + 315/U = 94.5$.
Subtracting: $35/U = 7 \implies U = 5	ext{ km/h}$.
$60/D + 40/5 = 12.5 \implies 60/D + 8 = 12.5 \implies 60/D = 4.5 \implies D = 60/4.5 = 40/3	ext{ km/h}$.
Speed of boat in still water $u =  rac{D + U}{2} =  rac{40/3 + 5}{2} =  rac{55}{6} \approx 9.17 \approx 9	ext{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A boat can go 15 km downstream and 8 km upstream in 2h. It can go 20 km downstream and 12 km upstream in 2h 50 min . What is the speed (in km/h) of the boat while going downstream?
questions.solution: $15/D + 8/U = 2$ and $20/D + 12/U = 17/6$.\nMultiply first by 3, second by 2: $45/D + 24/U = 6$ and $40/D + 24/U = 17/3$.\nSubtracting: $5/D = 6 - 17/3 = 1/3 \implies D = 15\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A boat can cover a distance of 7.2 km downstream and 3.2 km upstream in 2 hours. It can also cover 1.5 km downstream and 0.6 km upstream in 24 minutes. What is the speed of the boat when going downstream (in km/hr)?
questions.solution:
$7.2/D + 3.2/U = 2$ and $1.5/D + 0.6/U = 24/60 = 0.4$.
Multiply second by 4.8: $7.2/D + 2.88/U = 1.92$.
Subtract from first: $(3.2 - 2.88)/U = 2 - 1.92 \implies 0.32/U = 0.08 \implies U = 4	ext{ km/h}$.
$1.5/D + 0.6/4 = 0.4 \implies 1.5/D + 0.15 = 0.4 \implies 1.5/D = 0.25 \implies D = 6	ext{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A boat can go 5 km upstream 7\frac{1}{2} km downstream in 45 minutes. It can also go 5 km downstream and 2.5 km upstream in 25 minutes. How much time (in minutes) will it take to go 6 km upstream?
questions.solution:
$5/U + 7.5/D = 45/60 = 3/4$ and $2.5/U + 5/D = 25/60 = 5/12$.
Multiply second by 2: $5/U + 10/D = 10/12 = 5/6$.
Subtract first from this: $2.5/D = 5/6 - 3/4 = 1/12 \implies D = 30	ext{ km/h}$.
Then $5/U + 7.5/30 = 3/4 \implies 5/U + 1/4 = 3/4 \implies 5/U = 1/2 \implies U = 10	ext{ km/h}$.
Time to go 6 km upstream $=  rac{6}{10}	ext{ hours} = 36	ext{ minutes}$.

questions.questionText: A boat can go 5 km upstream and 7\frac{1}{2} km downstream in 45 minutes. It can also go 5 km downstream and 2.5 km upstream in 25 minute. How much time (in minutes) will it take to go 6 km downstream?
questions.solution: From previous question: $D = 30\text{ km/h}$.\nTime to go 6 km downstream $= \frac{6}{30}\text{ hours} = \frac{1}{5}\text{ hours} = 12\text{ minutes}$.

questions.questionText: A boat can go 3 km upstream and 5 km downstream in 55 minutes. It can also go 4 km upstream and 9 km downstream in 1 hour 25 minutes. In how much time (in hours) will it go 43.2 km downstream?
questions.solution:
$3/U + 5/D = 55/60 = 11/12$ and $4/U + 9/D = 85/60 = 17/12$.
Multiply first by 4, second by 3: $12/U + 20/D = 44/12$ and $12/U + 27/D = 51/12$.
Subtracting: $7/D = 7/12 \implies D = 12	ext{ km/h}$.
Time to go 43.2 km downstream $=  rac{43.2}{12} = 3.6	ext{ hours}$.

questions.questionText: A boat goes 27 km upstream and 33 km downstream in 6 hours. In the same time it can go 36 km upstream and 22 km downstream. How much time will it take to go 36 km upstream and 44 km downstream?
questions.solution:
$27/U + 33/D = 6$ and $36/U + 22/D = 6$.
Equating: $27/U + 33/D = 36/U + 22/D \implies 11/D = 9/U \implies D =  rac{11}{9}U$.
Substitute: $27/U + 33/(11U/9) = 6 \implies 27/U + 27/U = 6 \implies 54/U = 6 \implies U = 9	ext{ km/h}, D = 11	ext{ km/h}$.
Time for 36 km upstream and 44 km downstream $=  rac{36}{9} +  rac{44}{11} = 4 + 4 = 8	ext{ hours}$.

questions.questionText: A boat can travel 78 km upstream and back in a total of 32 hours. It can travel 15 km upstream and 52 km downstream in a total of 9 hours. How much distance will the boat cover in 12 hours in still water?
questions.solution:
$78/U + 78/D = 32$ and $15/U + 52/D = 9$.
Notice $52$ and $78$ are multiples of $13$ or $26$. Testing $D = 13$: $15/U + 52/13 = 15/U + 4 = 9 \implies 15/U = 5 \implies U = 3	ext{ km/h}$.
Check first: $78/3 + 78/13 = 26 + 6 = 32	ext{ hours}$ (Matches!).
Speed in still water $u =  rac{D + U}{2} =  rac{13 + 3}{2} = 8	ext{ km/h}$.
Distance covered in 12 hours $= 8 	imes 12 = 96	ext{ km}$.

questions.questionText: Abhi rows upstream a distance of 28 km in 4h and rows downstream a distance of 50 km in 2h. To row a distance of 44.8 km in still water, he will take:
questions.solution: $U = \frac{28}{4} = 7\text{ km/h}$, $D = \frac{50}{2} = 25\text{ km/h}$.\nSpeed in still water $u = \frac{25 + 7}{2} = 16\text{ km/h}$.\nTime to row 44.8 km $= \frac{44.8}{16} = 2.8\text{ hours}$.

questions.questionText: A person rows upstream a distance of 55 km in 5 hours and rows downstream a distance of 75 km in 3 hours. How much time will he take to cover a distance of 96 km in still water?
questions.solution: $U = \frac{55}{5} = 11\text{ km/h}$, $D = \frac{75}{3} = 25\text{ km/h}$.\nSpeed in still water $u = \frac{25 + 11}{2} = 18\text{ km/h}$.\nTime $= \frac{96}{18} = \frac{16}{3}\text{ hours} = 5\text{ hours } 20\text{ minutes}$.

questions.questionText: A boat travels 3 km upstream in 1 h and 1 km downstream in 12 min. How much time will it take for the boat to go 6 km in still water?
questions.solution: $U = \frac{3}{1} = 3\text{ km/h}$, $D = \frac{1}{12/60} = 5\text{ km/h}$.\nSpeed in still water $u = \frac{5 + 3}{2} = 4\text{ km/h}$.\nTime for 6 km $= \frac{6}{4} = 1.5\text{ hours} = 1\text{ h } 30\text{ min}$.

questions.questionText: A man can row a distance of 900 meters against the stream in 12 minutes and returns to the starting points in 9 minutes. What is the speed (in km/h) of the man in still water?
questions.solution: $U = \frac{900}{12 \times 60} = 1.25\text{ m/s} = 1.25 \times \frac{18}{5} = 4.5\text{ km/h}$.\n$D = \frac{900}{9 \times 60} = \frac{5}{3}\text{ m/s} = \frac{5}{3} \times \frac{18}{5} = 6\text{ km/h}$.\nSpeed in still water $u = \frac{6 + 4.5}{2} = 5.25\text{ km/h} = 5\frac{1}{4}\text{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A man's speed in still water is 4 km/h more than the speed of the current. If the man takes a total of 10 h to cover 45 km downstream and 35 km upstream, then the speed of the man in still water is:
questions.solution:
Let current speed be $v$, so $u = v + 4$. Then $D = u + v = 2v + 4$, $U = u - v = 4	ext{ km/h}$.
Time $=  rac{45}{2v+4} +  rac{35}{4} = 10 \implies  rac{45}{2v+4} = 10 - 8.75 = 1.25 =  rac{5}{4}$.
$2v + 4 = 36 \implies 2v = 32 \implies v = 16	ext{ km/h}$.
Speed in still water $u = 16 + 4 = 20	ext{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: The speed of a boat in still water is 6 km/h and the speed of the stream is 1.5 km/h. In going from point A to point B and returning to A, the boatman takes 2 hours 40 min. Find the distance between points A and B.
questions.solution: $D = 6 + 1.5 = 7.5\text{ km/h}, U = 6 - 1.5 = 4.5\text{ km/h}$.\n$\frac{d}{7.5} + \frac{d}{4.5} = 2\frac{2}{3} = \frac{8}{3} \implies \frac{2d}{15} + \frac{2d}{9} = \frac{8}{3} \implies d\left(\frac{3+5}{45}\right) = \frac{4}{3} \implies \frac{8d}{45} = \frac{4}{3} \implies d = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{45}{8} = 7.5\text{ km}$.

questions.questionText: A swimmer swims from a point P against the current for 6 min and then swims back along the current for next 6 min and reaches at a point Q. If the distance between P and Q is 120 m then the speed of the current (in km/h) is:
questions.solution:
Distance upstream $= (u - v) 	imes t$, distance downstream $= (u + v) 	imes t$.
Net distance $PQ = (u + v)t - (u - v)t = 2vt = 120	ext{ m}$.
$2v 	imes (6 	imes 60) = 120 \implies 2v 	imes 360 = 120 \implies v =  rac{120}{720} =  rac{1}{6}	ext{ m/s}$.
$v =  rac{1}{6} 	imes  rac{18}{5} =  rac{3}{5} = 0.6	ext{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: A boat takes 20 hours for travelling downstream from point A to point B and comes back to a midpoint C between A and B. The speed of the stream is 5 km/h and the speed of the boat in still water is 10 km/h. Find the distance between A and B (in km).
questions.solution: $D = 10 + 5 = 15\text{ km/h}, U = 10 - 5 = 5\text{ km/h}$.\nDistance $AB = d$, distance $BC = d/2$.\n$\frac{d}{15} + \frac{d/2}{5} = 20 \implies \frac{d}{15} + \frac{d}{10} = 20 \implies \frac{5d}{30} = 20 \implies \frac{d}{6} = 20 \implies d = 120\text{ km}$.

questions.questionText: A boat covers a round trip journey between two points A and B in a river in T hours. If its speed in still water becomes 2 times, it would take \frac{80}{161} T hours for the same journey. Find the ratio of its speed in still water to the speed of the river.

A person rowing a boat goes from J to K (upstream) and returns from K to J (downstream) in a total time of 15 hours. The distance between J and K is 300 AU. The time taken by a man to row a boat a distance of 9 km downstream is equal to the time taken by him to row a boat a distance of 3 km upstream. What is the approximate speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
$ rac{9}{D} =  rac{3}{U} \implies D = 3U$.
Total round trip time: $ rac{300}{U} +  rac{300}{3U} = 15 \implies  rac{300}{U} +  rac{100}{U} = 15 \implies  rac{400}{U} = 15 \implies U =  rac{400}{15} =  rac{80}{3}	ext{ km/h}$.
$D = 3 	imes  rac{80}{3} = 80	ext{ km/h}$.
Speed of boat in still water $u =  rac{D + U}{2} =  rac{80 + 26.67}{2} =  rac{106.67}{2} = 53.33	ext{ km/h}$.

questions.questionText: X, Y are two points in a river. Point P and Q divide the straight line XY into three equal parts. The river flows along XY and the time taken by a boat to row from X to Q and from Y to Q are in the ratio 4 : 5. The ratio of the speed of the boat downstream to that of the river current is equal to:
questions.solution:
$X$ to $Q$ is downstream with distance $2d$, $Y$ to $Q$ is upstream with distance $d$.
$t_1 =  rac{2d}{D}$, $t_2 =  rac{d}{U}$.
$ rac{t_1}{t_2} =  rac{2d/D}{d/U} =  rac{2U}{D} =  rac{4}{5} \implies  rac{U}{D} =  rac{2}{5} \implies D = 5k, U = 2k$.
River current speed $v =  rac{D - U}{2} =  rac{5k - 2k}{2} = 1.5k$.
Ratio of downstream speed to river current $=  rac{D}{v} =  rac{5k}{1.5k} =  rac{10}{3} = 10 : 3$.
